gcat-physical-100654
GCAT lists 2026-205D’s main body as an estimated 1.5 metres long; including its appendages, its overall span is an estimated 5 metres.
gcat-physical-36112
COSMOS 2457 [GLONASS-M] had a launch mass of about 1,450 kg. Its cataloged overall span, including appendages, is about 7.8 metres.
proba3-artificial-eclipse
This spacecraft is one half of Proba-3's eclipse-making pair. In 2025, the two flew 150 metres apart, with one blocking sunlight so the other could photograph the Sun's faint corona.
themis-auroral-trigger
This spacecraft belongs to THEMIS, the mission whose observations helped show that magnetic reconnection in Earth's magnetic tail can trigger sudden eruptions of space weather.
sentinel2-thirteen-bands
This Sentinel-2 satellite was built to view land and vegetation in 13 spectral bands. Its imager covers a strip of Earth 290 kilometres wide in one pass.
metop-gps-atmosphere
Metop's GRAS instrument uses GPS signals grazing Earth's atmosphere to study the air. Their bending and delay provide information about temperature and humidity.
gps-atomic-time
GPS uses atomic-clock time broadcast from its satellites. That shared timing helps synchronize power grids and communication networks as well as determine position.
gps-twice-a-day
The GPS constellation is designed around satellites that circle Earth twice a day, about 20,200 km above the surface.
galileo-four-clocks
First-generation Galileo spacecraft carry four atomic clocks: two hydrogen masers and two rubidium clocks. The two technologies give the navigation system a backup time source.
galileo-sos-return-link
Galileo’s search-and-rescue service can send an acknowledgement back to a compatible emergency beacon, telling the person in danger that their alert and location have been received.
galileo-third-first-sar
The third Galileo satellite was one of the first two in the constellation fitted to relay emergency-beacon signals. Its rescue repeater was first switched on for testing in January 2013.
qzss-asymmetric-eight
QZSS satellites in quasi-zenith orbits trace an uneven figure eight in their ground track. They move more slowly in the northern part of the orbit, spending longer near Japan.
qzss-disaster-broadcast
QZS-3 and QZS-4 were used to trial Japan’s satellite disaster-warning service in 2018. The service broadcasts information such as tsunami, earthquake and volcanic-eruption warnings.
iridium-four-neighbors
Iridium’s constellation is designed to link each network satellite to four neighbors. Calls and data can travel through that moving mesh in space before reaching a ground gateway.
iridium-aireon-aircraft
The Iridium NEXT constellation also hosts Aireon receivers that listen for aircraft ADS-B broadcasts. Together they allow air-traffic surveillance over oceans and polar regions.
starlink-laser-mesh
The Starlink constellation uses laser links between satellites to form an internet mesh in space.
oneweb-twelve-planes
OneWeb’s first-generation broadband constellation was designed around 12 orbital planes, with satellites flying about 1,200 km above Earth.
oneweb-two-per-day
The first-generation OneWeb constellation was built using an assembly-line approach that reached a production rate of two satellites a day.
o3b-name-origin
O3b’s name refers to the ‘Other 3 Billion’: the people in emerging countries its original mission aimed to connect to affordable broadband.
o3b-steerable-beams
The original O3b satellites were designed to use steerable Ka-band beams about 700 km wide, aiming broadband capacity at selected areas from medium Earth orbit.
gsat6-six-metre-antenna
GSAT-6 unfolded a six-metre S-band antenna in space. ISRO built it to create five communication spot beams over India.
gsat29-optical-testbed
GSAT-29 carried experimental optical communications equipment, Q/V-band communications and a high-resolution camera alongside its broadband payloads.
himawari-ahi
The camera on this spacecraft was designed to scan the whole visible disk of Earth every ten minutes, while revisiting Japan every two and a half minutes.
metop-ascat
This spacecraft carries a radar instrument that measures the ocean surface. Tiny ripples change the returning signal, letting scientists work out wind speed and direction.
metop-b-rescue
Alongside its weather instruments, this spacecraft carries equipment designed to relay emergency-beacon messages to search-and-rescue centres.
msg-rescue
This spacecraft belongs to the Meteosat Second Generation family, whose spacecraft also carry a repeater designed to relay distress calls from emergency beacons.
gk2a-rapid-scan
This spacecraft can image a movable 1,000 by 1,000 kilometre target region every two minutes, letting weather services request close attention to storms or volcanic eruptions.
gk2b-gems
This spacecraft carries GEMS, an instrument designed to measure pollutants including nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and ozone across East Asia eight times during daylight.
fengyun-lmi
This spacecraft carries a lightning-mapping instrument designed to follow storms by detecting flashes within clouds, between clouds and from clouds to the ground.
cartosat2b-stereo
This spacecraft was designed to steer its view up to 26 degrees along or across its path, allowing stereo images for mapping the ground in three dimensions.
insat3dr-night-fog
This spacecraft was equipped to image low cloud and fog at night using infrared light. It also carries a transponder for search-and-rescue services.
gcom-c-sgli
This spacecraft’s imager was built to observe 19 wavelength channels, from near-ultraviolet to thermal infrared, to study vegetation, clouds, snow and ice.
iceye-sar
This spacecraft is part of the ICEYE radar-satellite family. These spacecraft send their own radar pulses toward Earth, allowing imaging through cloud cover and after dark.
capella-acadia-sar
This spacecraft is an Acadia-class radar-imaging spacecraft. The family uses synthetic aperture radar to observe Earth through clouds and in darkness.
tdrs-space-relay
This spacecraft belongs to NASA’s TDRS family, built to relay data between low-orbiting spacecraft and ground stations so missions can communicate for much more of each orbit.
o3b-mpower-meo
This spacecraft belongs to SES’s O3b mPOWER communications system, designed around medium Earth orbits about 8,000 kilometres above the surface.
mev1-commercial-docking
In February 2020, this spacecraft docked with Intelsat 901 above geostationary orbit. It supplied propulsion to help the communications satellite return to service.
scatsat1-wind
This spacecraft was built to measure ocean-surface wind speed and direction with a Ku-band scatterometer, providing data for weather forecasts and cyclone detection and tracking.
